subject: RFI: model source attestations, relicensing scenarios, and pinning SLAs
messages:
From: Hannah Li <hli@fintechcorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@fintechcorp.com>
Cc: Dr. Eric Zhou <eric.zhou@fintechcorp.com>
Date: 2027-02-14T09:12:00Z
Subject: RFI: model source attestations, relicensing scenarios, and pinning SLAs

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for taking our RFI. We have a few focused compliance questions for your model catalog and licensing practices as part of our procurement packet. The items below are high priority for our legal and ML Ops teams — could you confirm and provide any supporting artifacts?

1) Open-source license compatibility: do you provide a per-model license matrix that lists upstream licenses (Apache 2.0, MIT, GPL variants, etc.) and a Redwood-assigned compatibility status for deployment in commercial products?
2) Provenance & SBOM: do you produce a machine-readable SBOM or provenance record for each model release (training data summary, checkpoints, transform scripts) and how do you handle 3rd-party component attestations?
3) Re-licensing / relicensing notice: in the event an upstream model changes license or an author requests relicensing, what notification cadence do you provide to customers who have pinned that model version?
4) Version pinning & emergency rollback: what SLAs and operational steps exist for customers that pin specific model versions but need emergency rollback due to a vulnerability or quality regression?
5) Derivative work policy: do you generate any downstream attribution/notice artifacts that should be included when deploying a model-derived feature in our product?

If you can provide short answers plus any attachments or links to artifacts, we'll triage internally and follow up with technical clarifications. Ideally within 3 business days.

Thanks,
Hannah
Lead Procurement Manager
FinTechCorp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Li <hli@fintechcorp.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-15T15:08:00Z
Subject: Re: RFI: model source attestations, relicensing scenarios, and pinning SLAs

Hi Hannah — appreciate the concise list. I've answered inline below and attached a short model-catalog summary, a machine-readable license matrix export, and our internal pinning process diagram. High-level answers below; please see attachments for artifacts.

1) License compatibility: Yes — we maintain a per-model license matrix that records the upstream declared license, any additional contributor terms we are aware of, and a Redwood disposition: "commercial-usable", "requires-notice", or "restricted". The attached License_Matrix_2027-02.csv is the canonical export. For borderline cases we flag models as "requires-notice" and provide suggested notice language.

2) Provenance & SBOM: For each catalog entry we publish a provenance document (SBOM-style CSV/JSON) covering checkpoint origin, model weights hash, tokenizer/version, major training corpora categories (not raw customer data), and a list of major training-framework dependencies and versions. We do not disclose raw training data; rather we provide metadata summaries and third-party component attestations where available (see model-catalog summary).

3) Re-licensing notices: If an upstream license changes or a reclaim/relicensing request occurs, we notify pinned customers via the Console and by email to the account billing/contact list. Notification cadence: immediate alert + follow-up within 48 business hours with a remediation plan.

4) Version pinning & emergency rollback: Customers can pin exact model-version IDs in their deployment config. For emergency rollback we provide a 4-hour initial response SLA for enterprise Dedicated/Private contracts (investigation and recommended mitigation), and a 24-hour coordinated rollback path to a compatible prior version (or fallback hosted variant). The attached diagram explains automated rollback vs manual remediation flows.

5) Derivative work and attribution: We provide suggested attribution/notice templates when a model's license requires notice. For models with restrictive clauses we include a deploy-time warning in the Console.

Attachments: Redwood_Model_Catalog_Summary.pdf, License_Matrix_2027-02.csv, version-pinning-process-diagram.png

Let me know if you want engineering-level exported artifacts (SBOM JSON) for a short list of candidate models — we can produce those under NDA.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Dr. Eric Zhou <eric.zhou@fintechcorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@fintechcorp.com>
Date: 2027-02-17T11:30:00Z
Subject: Re: RFI: model source attestations, relicensing scenarios, and pinning SLAs

Marissa — thanks for the quick answers and the attachments. A couple of technical clarifications from our ML Ops team:

- For SBOM-style exports, can you confirm the schema fields and whether you include the model-weights SHA256 and tokenizer-vocab hash? We need content-addressable identifiers.
- In relicensing cases where the upstream author adds a copyleft-like condition, do you have an approved legal playbook (e.g., migrate to a previous snapshot, apply transformation to remove offending components, or suspend the model for new requests)?

Also, is there a way to programmatically subscribe to relicensing alerts (webhook or API)? If yes, please provide the endpoint spec or example payload.

Thanks,
Eric
Director, ML Ops
FinTechCorp

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Dr. Eric Zhou <eric.zhou@fintechcorp.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-18T09:02:00Z
Subject: Re: RFI: model source attestations, relicensing scenarios, and pinning SLAs

Eric — quick answers from engineering/legal liaison below; attaching a short example SBOM JSON schema as a CSV-friendly table in the license matrix export and a sample webhook payload in the drive link.

- Content identifiers: yes — we publish canonical content hashes for model weights (SHA256) and tokenizer vocabulary (SHA256) in the SBOM. We also include a model-release manifest id and build-time metadata (framework and commit sha).
- Copyleft/relicensing playbook: Our standard playbook is: 1) notify pinned customers immediately; 2) assess whether the change creates a downstream compliance obligation; 3a) if remediable, offer a migration to a compatible prior snapshot with assisted rollback; 3b) if not remediable, place the affected model in a "suspended for new requests" state and offer substitutes and remediation options (license clearance, re-training) under enterprise support. We record each incident in an internal audit log and provide customers an incident summary.
- Programmatic alerts: Yes — enterprise customers can subscribe to a "model-status" webhook that sends events for: license_change, vuln_alert, signature_mismatch, and deprecation_notice. Example payload and topics are in the related_links Drive doc. Webhook delivery guarantees are best-effort with retry/backoff; for higher-assurance channels we recommend integrating our Console notifications + signed email digest.

Priyom (copied) — can you add anything about operational rollback times vs. customer pinning semantics?

Thanks,
Neha
Principal Product Manager, Catalog & Governance

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Dr. Eric Zhou <eric.zhou@fintechcorp.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-20T16:45:00Z
Subject: Re: RFI: model source attestations, relicensing scenarios, and pinning SLAs

Eric — adding a short operational note: when customers pin by version-id they retain read-only access to that exact artifact (weights + tokenizer). For Hosted customers we keep a pinned snapshot for 90 days by default (configurable under enterprise contracts); Dedicated/Private contracts can extend cold storage retention to 2+ years as part of the agreement. Emergency rollback timeline assumptions in enterprise plans: 4-hour triage window, 24-hour coordinated rollback to an alternative version, and 72-hour remediation target for complex licensing incidents requiring legal review. We can adjust these times in SROs for your procurement process.

If FinTechCorp wants the webhook spec and a sample SBOM JSON for three candidate models, say the names and we'll provision the artifacts under NDA.

— Priyom
Senior Product Engineer, Redwood Inference
